Two of this week's six questions were office-specific: "Cube Farm Traffic" only went up on HQ's whiteboard, and "Moving Upward" only went up on RTP's. Everyone else got all six questions. More on the two one-office questions below -- they're part of the decisiveness numbers like everything else, just excluded from the HQ/RTP comparison later on, since there's no second office's result to compare them to.

# How decisive were these results?

Five of six questions were a simple either-or, so those get the usual binomial test against a 50/50 split. The sixth, "Best Email Signoff," had four options, so it gets the chi-square goodness-of-fit test instead (see the [Week Daze](../20260909_weekdaze/index.html) post for why).


::: {.cell}

:::


**TL;DR:** Teams Meetings was the most one-sided call of the week -- Join right on time beat Start a few minutes early 69–21 (77%). Moving Upward was the closest thing to a real debate: Stairs edged Elevator 18–16, about as close to a coin flip as this poll has ever produced (p = 0.86) -- fittingly, it's also the one question only RTP got to weigh in on.

HQ and RTP picked the exact same winner on all four shared questions this week -- no flips, and the running flip tally holds at **11**.

The Alignment Index for this poll alone comes out to **0.9**, and the cumulative index sits at **0.89**. With total agreement on every winner and reasonably similar enthusiasm across the board, this was a quiet week for office tension.

# Do the procrastinators run hot?

"Wait until it's really a problem" swept EISD Tickets, and "Too Hot" swept Worst Office Temperature -- both landslides, and both questions drew almost identical crowds. Let's bound how much the "let it boil over" types overlap.


::: {.cell}

:::


Of the 92 overlapping voters, the ticket-procrastinating, thermostat-blaming crowd could be as small as 31 or as large as 56 people (34%–61%), versus about 41 (45%) expected if the two opinions were unrelated. Both landslides are large enough that the floor sits well above zero -- there's a real, forced overlap here, not just a coincidence of two big majorities.
